claims.value: lay keeper of the temple who guards obj-elder-scroll but is not the formal priest
claims.quote: He was a lay keeper of the temple — guardian of the scroll, not its formal priest — and he made that distinction in the way he spoke and in the small rituals he allowed in his rooms.

Lau fidgeted with a knot of string in his hands; he was fifteen and watched Mercy with the mixture of dislike for being told what to do and the hunger of someone trying to learn a trade that might save them both.

claims.value: has not been opened since the occupation began
claims.quote: "The room hasn't been opened since the occupation began," he said, as if stating a fact that would guard them from any lazy assumptions.

claims.value: brittle, foxed paper with marginal notes in different hands; the Elder will not let others touch it without negotiation
claims.quote: He hummed an old line, fingers worrying the edge of the scroll before he unfurled it. The paper was foxed and creased; marginal notes in different hands crowded some pages, and a faded thumbprint smudged one annotation. He would not let others touch it without a quiet negotiation — he set the scroll between them like a thing both alive and fragile and kept his hand over it until Mercy had bargained with the room.

claims.value: "they buried names in the under-floor"; "the men taken at the water's turn"
claims.quote: The Elder tapped the scroll, and then, in a voice like dry paper, offered two fragments that sat like hooks in the air: "they buried names in the under-floor," he said, and later, "the men taken at the water's turn."

claims.value: require talisman left under altar; promise to tell names found; two measures of rice to replace lock
claims.quote: An elder woman crossed her arms and said plainly: "We will let you search, if you leave a talisman under the altar and tell us any names you find. Also — the lock must be fixed afterward. Two measures of rice for the lock, and we will close the door again."

claims.value: left two measures of rice on the altar and placed a folded red talisman under the altar
claims.quote: Mercy set two measures of rice on the altar herself, the grain bright and ordinary under candlelight. She left a folded red talisman where the smoke would settle and, in a voice meant to be heard, promised to read aloud any names she found.
"I'll hold the talisman," he said quickly, eager in that messy way apprentices are when offered a task that looks important.

claims.value: marginal notes in the scroll may hide names; 'Names rubbed thin hide the worst parts.'
claims.quote: The Elder watched, his fingers touching marginalia with the same careful curiosity he'd used on the scroll. He hummed again, an old note that might be a blessing or might be a warning. ... The Elder folded the scroll back to a safe page and, in the hush that followed the bargain, added, almost to himself, "Mind what the marginal notes hide. Names rubbed thin hide the worst parts."

promises.promise: Mercy will search the locked room in the temple basement with witnesses and report any names back to the hall.
promises.quote: "You may search the basement locked room. But take witnesses and bring the names back to the hall."
